transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-10 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Nina Park (Redwood AE), Lucas Reed (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (CISO, Auriga), Ravi Patel (Infra Lead), Lena Ortiz (ML Platform Lead)

Summary (auto): initial security intake to surface gating controls for production inference. Need to confirm KMS model, SSO integration path, RBAC granularity, audit log retention windows and encrypted at-rest/backups.

[00:00] Nina (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for making time, i think we've got about 50 minutes, i'll do a quick intro then pass to Lucas for the technical bits. Maya, thanks for coordinating on your side.
[00:12] Maya (Auriga CISO): yep thanks, our execs want to move fast but we have strict controls; i'm here to make sure we don't miss compliance gates.
[00:18] Nina: perfect. quick context - Auriga's eval is around running inference for prod customer-facing features. you flagged a few big areas — encryption keys, sso, and audit logs? is that the right triage?
[00:27] Maya: yes exactly. also retention windows because some of our data is regulated under e-privacy and certain European regs.
[00:33] Ravi (Auriga Infra): and from infra, network topology and ability to use our KMS is huge; we prefer customer-managed keys if possible.
[00:38] Nina: understood. i'll hand off to Lucas to walk through hosting options and where the controls map.
[00:42] Lucas (Redwood SE): cool — hi all. i'll keep it high level then dig in. Redwood supports three deployment modes: hosted (our cloud API), dedicated (reserved GPU pools in our infra), and private (VPC or on-prem package). For each we can surface different controls.
[01:05] Lucas: hosted — easiest to get started, but by default keys are managed by Redwood. we do have envelope encryption and we can enable customer v-managed keys for enterprise tiers, though that has additional network/auth steps. some customers call that "bring-your-kms".
[01:25] Maya: when you say "bring-your-kms" do you mean we can point to our AWS KMS key? or do you require bringing HSM appliances?
[01:33] Lucas: good question — we support AWS KMS and GCP KMS integrations for keys at rest via a key wrap model. we also have an HSM-backed option for Private deployments where we can integrate with on-prem HSMs, but that typically requires a private package and some SAs to wire it into the key establishment flow.
[01:47] Ravi: so for hosted we could do an AWS CMK; is the key material ever held by Redwood?
[01:53] Lucas: in the envelope pattern, raw key material stays in your KMS; Redwood gets the wrapped key and uses it for short-lived decryption in memory. we don't persist unwrapped key material to disk. (note: some transcript words may be a little off - "envelope" sometimes spoken fast)
[02:08] Lena (ML Lead): and what about KV cache — we rely on prefix caching for latency. do cached tokens or KV store contain PII?
[02:15] Lucas: KV cache contains model context, which can include user input. for private/dedicated you can opt to keep caches in your VPC or ephemeral memory only. for hosted we have configurable retention and redaction.
[02:27] Maya: configurable retention — how granular? we need 90 days for debug logs, but anything with PII should be deleted in 7 days.
[02:32] Nina: quick note — we'll put that on the retention matrix action item, and Lucas will call out where logs vs payloads live.
[02:39] Lucas: sounds good. audit logs — we emit request-level logs, token counts, model versions, and access events. for enterprise tiers we can ship logs to customer S3 or to a SIEM via syslog/forwarder. retention and deletion policies can be set on the storage side.
[02:58] Ravi: SIEM forwarding is good — what about redaction? we want sensitive fields stripped before logs leave our environment.
[03:05] Lucas: we offer pre-shipping redaction hooks and a scrubber pipeline that can mask common PII patterns. it's rule-driven but we recommend customers run their own final scrubbers as well.
[03:16] Maya: SSO is another gate — we need SAML 2.0 with SCIM provisioning ideally, plus SSO enforced for system admins.
[03:24] Nina: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; for RBAC we have role templates but also custom roles. Lucas, can you share how RBAC maps to tokens and route-level controls?
[03:36] Lucas: sure — RBAC in the console maps to API tokens and role scopes. for example you can have "model-readonly", "deploy-admin", and "billing" roles. tokens can be restricted to endpoints and models. for Private deployments tokens can be further scoped to IP ranges.
[03:51] Lena: are tokens human-issued? or do you integrate with our OIDC provider for short-lived tokens?
[03:56] Lucas: both — we can mint short-lived tokens via our STS with OIDC or SAML assertion flows and issue ephemeral tokens that expire. that's standard for dedicated/private setups.
[04:09] Ravi: network — for private we need explicit egress rules and cert pinning; what's your recommended VPN/peering pattern?
[04:16] Lucas: commonly we do VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink; for stricter setups customers use an on-prem package where the inference runtime runs inside their network and only management plane talks out to Redwood. that removes egress concerns.
[04:30] Maya: for SOC2/ISO, can you send your attestations? we need the latest reports as part of vendor assessment.
[04:36] Nina: absolutely — i'll send SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 snapshots. note: sometimes the naming in our docs is older, but i'll include the attestation PDFs and a short matrix mapping controls to your requirements.
[04:48] Maya: retention of logs and how long you retain query payloads for hosted mode — can customers force delete?
[04:54] Lucas: in hosted there is a standard retention policy (30 days for request payloads by default) but enterprise tiers let you set custom retention or opt out of retention entirely by enabling no-persist mode, though that impacts traceability and debugging. for dedicated/private it's controllable on your side.
[05:11] Maya: is there a way to request deletion for a particular user event (like a right-to-be-forgotten flow)?
[05:16] Lucas: yes — we support subject access deletion requests; for hosted we have a ticketed workflow where we validate and remove across indexed stores. for private, customers handle deletion locally.
[05:27] Ravi: backups — if you integrate with our KMS do backups get encrypted under our CMK as well?
[05:33] Lucas: yes, when integrated with a customer CMK, snapshots and backups are wrapped with the same key material per the envelope model.
[05:40] Lena: audit evidence — can we get raw access logs for a rolling 12 months?
[05:44] Lucas: we generally provide access logs for 12 months for enterprise customers; long-tail retention can be configured but may incur costs.
[05:51] Maya: we also have vendor requirements around penetration tests and vuln disclosure. do you do third-party pen tests?
[05:57] Nina: we do periodic third-party pentests and maintain a vuln disclosure program with a security@ email. i'll include the latest pentest summary in the packet.
[06:07] Maya: okay good. are there any roadblocks you expect for us to use customer-managed KMS in hosted?
[06:13] Lucas: the main work is network auth between Redwood's control plane and your KMS, and ensuring roles/assume-role patterns are set up. it can be done, but there are a couple of ops steps; we'll document them.
[06:24] Ravi: latency implications — if the key wrapping call adds round trips at init is that significant?
[06:30] Lucas: we cache the unwrapped symmetric key for short-lived sessions in memory; the extra handshake is minimal and amortized over many requests. worst case you see a small cold-start on a model host.
[06:41] Lena: model rollback and canary — we want to make sure audit trails show which model version served which request.
[06:47] Lucas: we surface model version in the logs and traces and can pin model versions per route; canary deploys are supported and marked in audit logs.
[06:56] Maya: any compliance certifications for Dedicated nodes?
[06:59] Lucas: dedicated pools come under our corporate SOC and we extend control evidence for customer-dedicated instances; for private, you get even more control because runtime is in your network.
[07:10] Nina: quick check — are there specific red flags that would force you to insist on private/on-prem? Maya?
[07:17] Maya: if we can't get customer-managed keys and we can't ensure PII redaction before logs egress, that's a showstopper. also, inability to SCIM + enforce SSO for admin users is a big no.
[07:29] Ravi: and for infra — if network ports/peering patterns require unsupported changes to our VPC, we might prefer the on-prem appliance.
[07:36] Nina: understood. i'll capture that as acceptance criteria.
[07:40] Lucas: one operational note — for private deployment we provide the runtime bundle and a management agent; we still provide the control plane for model catalog and rollouts but the control plane can be run in a customer VPC for strict air-gap needs.
[07:55] Lena: what about data residency — we have customers in EU and APAC and need region-specific hosting. can you guarantee region pinning?
[08:02] Lucas: yes, we support region pinning via deployment policies — hosted models can be pinned to specific region clusters; dedicated/private gives you stronger guarantees.
[08:12] Maya: anything else about audit logs? specifically chain-of-custody for logs if requested in an audit.
[08:18] Lucas: we can provide signed log exports and integrate with your SIEM for immutable storage; for deeper chain-of-custody we recommend storage in your own S3 with object-lock enabled.
[08:30] Nina: okay we're about midway through — any other controls?
[08:34] Maya: one more — staff access for Redwood engineers. do you have jumpbox access or do you use bastion with MFA?
[08:40] Lucas: Redwood support accesses customer instances through a gated bastion with SSO + MFA and just-in-time access workflows; all sessions are recorded and logged. for private on-prem installs we can adapt to your access model.
[08:53] Ravi: can you show evidence of that? session logs or an example audit?
[08:58] Nina: yes i'll include sample support access audit excerpts.
[09:02] (short crosstalk, someone briefly muted)
[09:10] Maya: timeline — we're looking at a pilot in Q1. decision criteria: keys must be customer-managed or private, SSO must be enforced for admins, audit logs retention 12 months with 90-day quick access, and data retention rules respected per user type.
[09:29] Nina: sounds actionable. i'll summarize next steps: send attestation docs, schedule Lucas + Ravi deep dive about networking and KMS wiring, and Maya will share retention matrix.
[09:40] Lucas: i'll also draft the change list for the private package if you end up on that path.
[09:45] Lena: any rough cost delta between dedicated with BYOK and private?
[09:50] Nina: quick thumb — dedicated with BYOK typically 15-30% premium over hosted enterprise pricing; private/on-prem has a higher base fee and professional services. we'll follow up with numbers.
[09:59] Maya: ok thanks everyone.
[10:02] Nina: one last thing — security contact? i'll send to security@auriga and to your procurement.
[10:08] Maya: please copy me and Ravi.
[10:10] Nina: will do. thanks all.

Recap / explicit next steps (auto):
- Redwood (Nina) to send SOC2 Type II + ISO27001 snaps, pentest summary, support access audit excerpts, and security whitepaper.
- Redwood (Lucas) to prepare network diagram and KMS integration steps for AWS KMS and HSM notes.
- Auriga (Maya) to provide data classification and retention requirements spreadsheet.
- Schedule 90-min SE deep dive (Lucas + Ravi) to discuss VPC peering, Private package, and certs.

End of transcript.
